why: The ODE method is a general mathematical technique for proving convergence of stochastic approximation algorithms, not a general theory of learning or an education-specific research method.

ODLE is a technology-system architecture and component-engineering framework for building open distributed learning environments, not a general explanatory theory of how people learn or a method for studying learning.
OD3R is a course-specific five-stage instructional sequence for integrating biochemistry lectures and laboratory work, not a general explanatory learning theory.
This is a course-specific implementation of the OD3R sequence for undergraduate biochemistry students, with stage activities and domain mappings tailored to that setting.

The report and practical-skills instruments are rubric-based assessments with explicit criteria and performance levels, while the questionnaire is a narrower assessment instrument rather than a distinct instructional element.
The Oral Disease Recognition Scale is a named, previously validated assessment instrument rather than a general instructional element.
name: Oral Disease Recognition Scale (ODRS) with seven clinical cases
product_description: A validated seven-case clinical assessment instrument that presents oral-disease histories and images with five diagnosis options and confidence ratings to measure oral disease recognition and diagnostic-confidence calibration in dental learners and dentists.

why: This is a small pilot's proposed model for scoring clinical reasoning in one oral-debrief OSCE assessment, not a general learning theory or broadly reusable theory of learning.
